## Summary

Asked what happens if both routes are needed for item 5, and revised the recommendation: my earlier choose-your-goal framing was too binary. The two routes are layers, not alternatives, and both are reachable. The architectural move that makes it work is that the determinism law is only broken when inference runs INSIDE the fold; it is not broken when inference runs outside and its output is recorded as ordinary events, because the fold then remains a pure function of the event set and the non-determinism sits in a producer where it is auditable. That is the same trick sofar already rests on — it never infers, it folds. So enrichment event types live in packages/schema and producers are pluggable: an agent mid-session, free and needing no rule change, and an opt-in semantic pass that costs money and needs a Decision, both emitting the same event types with the producer stamped on each so either can be dropped or recomputed independently. This also shrinks the rule change substantially: if the semantic pass is an explicit user-invoked command rather than a runtime dependency, the Decision needed is narrow, permitting a model call only from that command while the engine, hooks, MCP server and fold never make one, so a default install still makes zero model calls and the no-key property and hot path stay intact, which is what the invariant was actually protecting. Recorded why the agent route must still go first, as de-risking rather than compromise: it defines the event types, index and query surface so the semantic producer becomes just another writer into tested machinery; it produces labelled data, turning are-embeddings-actually-better into a measurable question against declared links as ground truth; and it costs nothing and blocks nothing.

## Next action

Start item 5 with the agent-emitted layer, since it needs no ruling: define the enrichment event types in packages/schema with a producer field stamped on every event, and generalise the existing declared-relevance mechanism that sofar_log_decision guard and core index-tier1 already implement. Defer the semantic producer until there are real declared links to measure it against, then log a narrowly scoped Decision permitting a model call only from an explicit opt-in command, naming SPEC Architectural invariants and felt-cost D3.
